findings.description: The 'data' bucket has no ACL restriction, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and no restrictive bucket policy, and is explicitly annotated as public. Anonymous principals can potentially read (and with a public-write ACL, modify) its contents, which include a customer master file.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects including customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this publicly exposed bucket would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects overwritten or deleted by an attacker exploiting the public access cannot be recovered and no tamper evidence is retained.

A customer master spreadsheet (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the unencrypted, publicly accessible 'data' bucket with no per-object kms_key_id or server-side encryption, directly exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, eliminating the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so financial objects can be overwritten or deleted with no recovery path or tamper evidence.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so the private ACL is the only control preventing exposure; a later ACL or policy change could publish financial data without any account-level guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operations data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this bucket is not auditable for forensic or compliance purposes.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block protects this bucket, leaving it dependent solely on the ACL setting to prevent public exposure.
The data science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so potentially sensitive datasets are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against future public ACLs or bucket policies.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the central log bucket, so a future ACL or policy change could expose audit log data that records access to the other buckets.

The central log bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no object lock or MFA delete, so audit log data relied upon for incident response can be destroyed wholesale by anyone able to delete the bucket.
